technical_and_design_decisions: The increment is implemented on the existing Spring XD codebase (master branch), which is built on Spring Boot and Spring Integration; development targets the project's current technology stack and Gradle build system.

U2 (lazy job module lifecycle): implement bootstrap-on-launch by hooking module deployment into the job launch request path, and shut down the module context on job completion using a completion listener with reference counting so shared modules are not prematurely closed.

U4 (metrics): integrate with Spring Boot Actuator's MetricRepository export() mechanism (MetricRepositoryAutoConfiguration) by implementing a metric reader/exporter inside XD containers so each deployed module/app publishes its Boot metrics to XD's monitoring channel.

U5 (module options): adopt Spring Boot's configuration metadata (spring-boot-configuration-processor / configuration-metadata.json) and relaxed property binding so module options are resolved purely through Boot PropertySource ordering; XD-maintained module option metadata is removed from the core runtime classpath.

U6 (externalized configuration): introduce centralized externalized configuration based on a Spring Cloud Config-style server with a Git-backed property repository; XD-Admin and XD-Container act as config clients resolving environment-specific properties at startup.

U7 (Rabbit message bus performance): use the RabbitMQ management plugin plus JVM profiling and targeted throughput benchmarks (varying prefetch, ack mode, durability, concurrency, connection/channel caching) to isolate the bottleneck before applying a focused fix in the Rabbit message bus binding.
U8 (CI migration): migrate Jenkins-based CI for the master branch to AWS EC2 using pre-built AMIs containing the build toolchain, with EC2 instances provisioned on demand for build agents.

U1 (benchmarks): define repeatable benchmark scenarios for representative XD topologies (stream and batch), execute them on documented EC2-based cluster hardware, and publish results with full infrastructure specifics in the project's Asciidoc reference documentation.
All documentation is maintained as Asciidoc in the project repository; unit and integration tests accompany every code change.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are effort in work-hours, not elapsed calendar time.
The existing Spring XD development environment, Gradle build, source repository, and test infrastructure are available and functional.
An AWS account with permissions to create EC2 instances/AMIs and a Jenkins CI server are available for U1 and U8.
RabbitMQ broker and a representative multi-node XD cluster environment are available for benchmarking and performance troubleshooting (U1, U7).
All eight user stories are delivered together as one software increment; code review effort by peers is not counted since a single developer performs the work.
Unit and integration testing effort is included within each development activity; no external teams or approvals block progress.
Third-party library upgrades required by the changes (e.g., Spring Boot/Cloud versions) are minor and included in the activity estimates.
The generic Spring Framework background in the specification (including Spring Framework 6 / Java 17) is contextual; the increment targets the existing Spring XD stack and its supported Java version.
